articles.title: Teen Charged Over Alleged Plot to Attack Hindu Temple Near Chicago
articles.excerpt: Police say co-workers reported an alleged manifesto and a jammed rifle on Sunday, leading to the arrest of a 19-year-old Palatine man now held pending trial.
articles.nri_angle: The alleged target was a Hindu temple serving Indian-American worshippers near Chicago, and community groups are urging vigilance and direct reporting of threats to police.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Saudi Court Overturns Death Sentence Over Deleted Facebook Comment
articles.excerpt: Saudi Arabia's Supreme Court set aside the death sentence of Sri Lankan worker Anojan Sivarasa, 27, but whether he still faces prison or can return home remains unclear.
articles.nri_angle: A migrant-worker speech case in the Gulf with direct relevance to South Asian workers abroad and the consular help available to them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Andhra University Takes Centenary to US Alumni, Houston MoU Discussed
articles.excerpt: Vice-Chancellor G.P. Raja Sekhar's delegation drew 200 alumni in Sugar Land, discussed a University of Houston MoU, and heads to Penn State and New Jersey.
articles.image_caption: Andhra University in Visakhapatnam. The university is taking its centenary celebrations to US alumni, with a Houston MoU discussed.
articles.nri_angle: US alumni are asked for mentoring, partnerships and endowments, with a final open meeting in Fords, New Jersey, on October 17.

articles.title: Chennai-Born Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal Backs India Protests Over Voter Roll Deletions
articles.excerpt: The Washington Democrat, the first US lawmaker to comment on India's SIR exercise, cited reports of 13 crore names removed from draft rolls and backed non-violent protests demanding the election chief's resignation.
articles.image_caption: US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal is pictured in a composite image alongside protesters in India. Jayapal backed non-violent protests over deletions from draft electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision.
articles.nri_angle: The most prominent Chennai-born member of the US Congress has intervened in India's voter-roll dispute, linking it to the US voting-rights debate ahead of her own midterm re-election fight against another Indian American.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chinese Parts Are Fuelling Houthi Bid to Build Missiles That Reach Israel, Saudi Arabia
articles.excerpt: Intercepted shipments of Chinese missile motors, fins and heat-shield material point to a Houthi effort to build a version of Iran's Kheibar Shekan, though how far production has advanced is unclear.
articles.image_caption: Image: @MarioNawfal via X
articles.nri_angle: A more capable Houthi missile force threatens Gulf states hosting millions of Indian workers and the energy routes India depends on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Ships Sink Near Strait of Hormuz as Attacks on Vessels Intensify
articles.excerpt: The Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride sank after a projectile strike and fire, while the bulk carrier Cape Dao, hit on September 23, was reported sinking after a failed rescue attempt.
articles.image_caption: The Strait of Hormuz and the Musandam Peninsula, seen in a satellite image. Two commercial vessels sank near the strait as attacks on shipping intensified.
articles.nri_angle: Hormuz disruption raises crude, freight and Gulf-route airfare costs for India and the millions of Indian workers in Gulf states.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Florida Can Enforce Ban on Social Media Accounts for Children Under 14
articles.excerpt: An appeals court panel vacated the injunction blocking HB 3, finding the law targets addictive platform features rather than speech — and clearing Florida to act against accounts held by younger children.
articles.image_caption: The Elbert P. Tuttle US Courthouse in Atlanta, home of the 11th US Circuit Court of Appeals. A panel of that court ruled Florida can enforce its ban on social media accounts for children under 14.

articles.title: Peter Nagy, Gallerist Who Put Indian Contemporary Art on World Map, Dies at 67
articles.excerpt: The American-born founder of Nature Morte, who moved to Delhi in 1992 and championed Bharti Kher, Jitish Kallat and a generation of Indian artists, has died after a long illness.
articles.image_caption: Peter Nagy pictured in 2014 at his Eisbox Projects exhibition. Nagy, the Nature Morte founder who championed Indian contemporary art, died on October 13 at the age of 67.
articles.nri_angle: Nagy linked the New York and Indian art worlds for three decades, shaping how Indian contemporary art — and the diaspora collectors who buy it — is seen globally.

articles.title: East Brunswick Declares October Hindu Heritage Month, Sets Two Diwali Celebrations
articles.excerpt: Mayor Brad Cohen and the Township Council presented the proclamation on October 12; a Mega Diwali festival on October 24 and a municipal lighting ceremony on October 30 are open to all residents.

articles.nri_angle: East Brunswick is a Middlesex County hub for Indian Americans; the proclamation and two public Diwali events give local families civic recognition plus concrete dates to attend.
